core.title: Write flow router guards only in the declarative guard grammar
core.given: A user/system flow flow router in a plan artifact declares guard expressions
core.when: the planner writes or edits a guard, or the plan reaches the CONFIRM phase
core.then: Every guard uses only the stack's declarative guard grammar (allowed operators and presence-test form from the profile) over only allowed inputs — action/request inputs, an explicit state snapshot, and a completed user/system flow result only at a declared route boundary — with no executable code, side effect, or non-deterministic input beyond that grammar.
prefer: Pure comparisons and boolean combinations over declared input and snapshot fields.
The grammar's presence-test form to test whether a field is present.
Pass needed data through the explicit state snapshot.
avoid: Dynamic evaluation or arbitrary executable code in a guard: any call other than the grammar's presence test, imports, anonymous functions, method calls, comprehension or iteration expressions. Plain references to allowed input fields are fine.
Side effects or non-deterministic inputs (time, randomness, environment, I/O).
Reading a user/system flow result that is not completed or is outside a declared route boundary.
Disguising disallowed tokens to get past the guard-grammar check.
core.why: Guards decide routing. Declarative, deterministic, side-effect-free guards keep routes reproducible and statically checkable; raw dynamic evaluation allows arbitrary code execution.
evidence: The CONFIRM-phase grammar check passes for every flow router guard.
Every guard token is an allowed input reference, a literal, or one of the grammar's allowed operator or presence-test forms.
On failure, the report names the flow router, the guard, the expression, the invalid token, and the reason.
verification: Grammar-conformance check over flow router guard expressions (subject: flow routers in plan artifacts): every token must be an allowed input reference, a literal, or one of the grammar's allowed forms; any other call, operator, or executable construct is an invalid-token finding.
Allowed inputs are only the grammar's declared input kinds: action/request inputs, an explicit state snapshot, and a completed user/system flow result only at declared route boundaries.
Phase CONFIRM, enforcement confirm-blocking: a finding blocks plan confirmation. Severity 3, disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode.
Scope: every flow router guard, changed or not. The guard-added/modified change trigger is an early extra trigger, not a required condition; unchanged guards are still checked at CONFIRM.
On failure the report identifies the flow router, the guard, the expression, the invalid token, and the reason; the exact field names are the realization's failure-evidence schema.

fires: A planner adds or edits a guard expression on a user/system flow flow router in a plan artifact.
CONFIRM validation runs over a plan whose flow routers contain guards, including guards that were not changed.
A guard uses arbitrary executable code (dynamic evaluation, a call other than the grammar's presence test, an anonymous function, a method call) or a token outside the grammar's allowed set.
A guard reads a user/system flow result that is not completed or is not at a declared route boundary.
The CONFIRM grammar check reports an invalid token in a flow router guard.
doesNotFire: Plans or user/system flows that declare no flow router guard expressions.
Plan prose or acceptance text that is not a flow router guard expression.

profileRequirements.meaning: The exact declarative grammar of routing-guard expressions in plan artifacts: the allowed input kinds, the allowed operators, and the presence-test call form. The core's 'declarative guard grammar' is this closed set; anything outside it is an invalid token.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Inputs: action/request inputs, an explicit state snapshot, and a completed UserSystemFlowResult only at declared route boundaries. Operators: == != < <= > >= and or not exists(field) in.

neutralityNotes: User/system flow, flow router, user/system flow result, route boundary and the CONFIRM phase are plan-artifact schema concepts shared across ATDD stacks, not stack machinery, so they stay in the core; a stack with a different plan vocabulary supplies its concrete grammar through the proposed idiom.plan_syntax#guard_grammar key. The Bun guard-expression tokens (and, or, not, in, exists(field)) are host-language spellings and live only in the profile value. Python-named forbidden constructs (raw eval, lambda, comprehension) are generalized to neutral forms covering the same forbidden set; the concrete spellings remain in bun.json as the reference example. Validator and finding ids and the failure-report field names are bunOnly. The Bun source names no path glob for flow routers, so no path or placement profile key is required.
